verdicts.why: He is asking a meta question in English and the Latin 'alayhi salmik' is likely engine garble of allah ysallmek; her 'Yes' answers whether to reply, with no voiced fix, so there is no defensible slip.
Her 'خلاص؟' only asks if he is done and he changed the hour himself; a wrong clock time is a fact, not a grammar slip, and the chat line alone cannot make it a correction (GR-19).
He was asking a question ('Is it بنقلق?') and بنقلق 'we worry' is valid; she offered the adjective or 'I worry' as options, which the brief treats as a question / both-forms-fine, not a slip.
He asked how to say 'taking care' and Amal supplied ديرت بالي out loud: a didn't-know (vocab-A, signal asked, tier 0) that the brief says to write.
Her voiced 'لا لا لا يا حرام' is sympathy for the fiancée, and her el-subu7 exists only in chat (GR-19); الصباح is a real Arabic word for morning, so a let-pass error is not convincing.
He said he forgot the word for sky ('أنا نسيته') and Amal voiced سما: a didn't-know row (vocab-A, asked, tier 0).
غيم is a valid collective for clouds, her line is engine garble ('فئة واحدة؟'), and his move to غيوم got only 'مم', so there is no clear voiced fix of a wrong word.
'Is it طيور?' is a question, she only asked which he meant, and he supplied طيارات himself, so under the brief it is neither a slip nor a supplied word.
Asked how to say it's dark, he said 'أنا نسيت' and Amal voiced عتمة: a didn't-know row (vocab-A, asked, tier 0).
For 'isn't here' he said مش فيهن/ما فيهن and Amal voiced مش هون and explained 'في is not is, في is there is', a clear voiced grammar correction he then accepted.
The closing line is likely engine garble (e.g. العافية فيكي / يعافيكي) and her يعطيك العافية reads as her own goodbye with no fix signal, so no slip can be defended.
